newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland blesses Tesco's Irish buy.
newsitem.headline: Ireland blesses Tesco's Irish buy.

text.p: Ireland gave its blessing to Tesco's 630 million Irish pound ($991.3 million) grocery chain acquisition on Wednesday after a meeting between Tesco chief executive Terry Leahy and an Irish government minister in Dublin.
"I called this meeting because this is a merger which will have considerable impact on Ireland," Minister for Enterprise and Employment Richard Bruton told reporters.
Britain's leading supermarket chain Tesco announced that it was acquiring Ireland's biggest grocery chain from Associated British Foods (ABF) for 630 million pounds on March 21.
"It was a satisfactory meeting and we addressed many of the concerns, agreed a number of things with Tesco and they made a number of commitments," Bruton said.

He said it was a very constructive meeting and he was pleased with Tesco's understanding of the strengths of the Irish market. "They are keen to work with Irish suppliers and the Irish workforce," Bruton said.
Some of the commitments included expanding the business, honouring existing commitments to employees in terms of pay and conditions and fostering new and emerging Irish suppliers, he said.
Tesco also agreed to honour the obligations set out in the Restrictive Practices (Groceries) Order 1987, including on credit terms and below cost selling.

"The Grocery Order was renewed last for a further two years and it is currently under review in the merger and competition review as part of the very broad independent review of competition law," Bruton said.
The deal is the largest ever in the Irish grocery trade and gives Tesco a 26 percent share of the market in the Irish Republic and 30 percent in Northern Ireland.
Tesco will take control of 75 Quinnsworth and Crazy Prices stores in the Republic as well as 34 stores in Northern Ireland trading under a variety of names.
At the time of the announcement Leahy reassured suppliers, distributors and the 8,300 Irish staff that there was more to gain than lose by the takeover and that the move would be positive for them.
